articles.title: Nepal tunnel survivor finds solace in village homecoming
articles.summary: After being trapped for nine days in a hydropower tunnel collapse, Sanjay Sah was rescued and returned to his village, where his family welcomed him. His homecoming brings a moment of relief amid the ongoing grief in the community, which is still mourning the workers who remain missing from the same disaster that occurred last month. The incident highlights the dangers faced by laborers in Nepal’s expanding hydro‑energy projects and the emotional toll on families awaiting news of their loved ones.

articles.title: Flood blocks Jajarkot-Dolpa road, sweeps away homes and shops
articles.summary: Heavy torrential rain caused severe flooding in the Nalgad area of Jajarkot district, Nepal. The flood inundated the Bheri Corridor, blocking the Jajarkot‑Dolpa road and halting transport along this vital route. Numerous homes, shops and other structures were swept away or heavily damaged, displacing residents and disrupting local commerce. Relief efforts are being mobilised as authorities assess the extent of the damage and plan for reconstruction of the road and affected properties.

articles.title: Nepal Airlines jet grounded in Japan, disrupting international flights
articles.summary: A Nepal Airlines wide‑body jet was forced to remain at Narita Airport in Japan after an engine problem forced the aircraft, carrying 226 passengers, to be grounded. The incident has halted the airline’s only operational wide‑body aircraft, disrupting its scheduled international services, including flights to Doha, which are now at risk of cancellation. Nepal Airlines is working with authorities to resolve the issue and arrange alternative transport for passengers.

articles.title: Beijing to ban drone possession, storage from November 15
articles.summary: Beijing announced that from November 15 it will prohibit the possession and storage of drones, aiming to strengthen airspace security. The regulation allows limited exemptions for emergency services, research, industrial activities and other authorized operations. The move reflects a broader effort by Chinese authorities to tighten control over unmanned aerial vehicles.

articles.title: US approves $1m forensic support for Nepal flood victim identification
articles.summary: The United States has approved an additional $1 million to support forensic efforts for identifying victims of recent floods in Nepal. This new allocation brings total U.S. humanitarian, health, and forensic assistance for flood relief in Nepal to over $5 million, aiming to improve victim identification and support affected communities.

articles.title: Himalayas approaching tipping point, millions of livelihoods at stake: Report
articles.summary: A new report warns that accelerating glacier melt in the Hindu Kush-Himalaya region is pushing the Himalayas toward a tipping point. The rapid loss of ice threatens water security for millions downstream and raises the risk of catastrophic glacial lake outburst floods, endangering livelihoods across Nepal, India, Bhutan, Pakistan and China. The findings call for urgent climate mitigation and adaptation measures to protect vulnerable communities and preserve the region’s water resources.

articles.title: Diplomacy stumbles with postponement of meeting on Strait of Hormuz proposal
articles.summary: A meeting on the Strait of Hormuz proposal was postponed at the request of some regional countries, following a joint decision by Tehran and Muscat, according to Iran’s Fars news agency citing a foreign ministry official.

articles.title: Deuba faction cracks as 31 leaders line up behind Thapa
articles.summary: 31 leaders from the Deuba faction have defected to support Gagan Thapa, dealing a blow to Sher Bahadur Deuba's push for a parallel convention.

articles.title: Finance Minister Wagle to visit India on September 17-18
articles.summary: Finance Minister Wagle will travel to India on September 17-18, marking the first high‑level Nepal‑India visit since the devastating floods that struck Nepal on August 26.

articles.title: India approves additional 654 MW power exports to Nepal
articles.summary: India has approved an additional 654 megawatts of electricity exports to Nepal to alleviate the latter's winter power shortages. The extra supply comes after recent floods damaged Nepal's hydropower plants and transmission lines, leaving the country vulnerable to energy deficits during the colder months. The increased import is expected to stabilize Nepal's grid and support households and businesses until repairs are completed.

articles.title: Nepal begins overhaul of school curriculum, with AI and indigenous knowledge in focus
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has launched a nationwide consultation to revamp the school curriculum, aiming to incorporate artificial intelligence, disaster preparedness, entrepreneurship, and indigenous knowledge. The initiative seeks input from educators, experts, and local communities to create a modern, resilient education system that reflects both technological advancement and cultural heritage. The overhaul is positioned as a step toward preparing students for future challenges while preserving Nepal's diverse traditions.

articles.title: Flood survivors face water shortages, disease risk in crowded holding centres
articles.summary: Over 3,600 flood survivors are staying in 37 holding centres across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts, facing water shortages and disease risk.

articles.title: Why fixing Nepal’s government takes more than just copying the rulebook
articles.summary: The article argues that Nepal's attempts to reform its bureaucracy are insufficient as public problems become more complex and citizens expect quicker, more transparent services. Simply copying existing rulebooks cannot address the systemic issues, and deeper, innovative changes are needed to meet modern governance demands.

articles.title: How Nepal can take the global lead on Himalayan climate strategy
articles.summary: The article argues that Nepal can become a global leader in Himalayan climate strategy by adopting predictive monitoring, resilient engineering, and managed retreat rather than relying on compensation schemes. By leveraging its unique mountainous terrain and vulnerable communities, Nepal can showcase innovative approaches that protect ecosystems, safeguard livelihoods, and influence international climate negotiations. The piece highlights the potential for Nepal’s policies to serve as a model for other vulnerable mountain nations, urging collaboration with global bodies such as the UNFCCC and development partners to scale these solutions.

articles.title: Why the government must be stopped from chaining the central bank governor
articles.summary: The article warns that recent amendments to the Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) Bill could undermine the country's monetary stability and erode the regulatory independence of the central bank. It argues that the government's proposed powers to chain or control the central bank governor threaten the credibility of monetary policy, risk inflationary pressures, and may deter foreign investment. The piece calls for immediate opposition to the bill, emphasizing the need to preserve the central bank’s autonomy to safeguard the economy.

articles.title: Private sector bears bulk of Bhotekoshi flood losses
articles.summary: A preliminary government assessment of the recent Bhotekoshi River flood estimates total damage and economic losses at roughly Rs408 billion. The disaster affected nearly 4,800 private‑sector businesses and 7,570 homes, while also damaging 13 hydropower projects and five solar power plants. The report highlights that the private sector is bearing the majority of the financial burden from the flood.

articles.title: The ’80s are trending. But AI nostalgia comes with a hidden environmental cost
articles.summary: A new wave of AI‑generated images styled after the 1980s is sweeping social media, but each picture consumes significant computing power, electricity and cooling. Experts warn that the cumulative energy demand of these seemingly innocuous posts adds to AI’s already sizable carbon footprint. The article cites data from major AI image generators such as OpenAI’s DALL·E, Midjourney and Google’s Imagen, highlighting how the surge in demand for retro‑styled visuals could increase emissions unless greener hardware or renewable energy sources are adopted. Environmental groups and technologists call for transparency about the hidden cost and for developers to optimise models for efficiency. While the trend fuels creativity, the piece underscores the need to balance digital culture with climate responsibility.

articles.title: After the floods, Nepal’s survivors face the uncertainty of starting over
articles.summary: Thousands of displaced people in Nepal are struggling to start over after floods destroyed homes and shelters, with winter approaching.

articles.title: 472 undocumented workers, including Nepalis, detained in Kuala Lumpur raids
articles.summary: 472 undocumented workers, including Nepalis, were detained in Kuala Lumpur raids as part of an extended migrant repatriation programme.

articles.title: Foreign stars raise the bar for Nepal’s volleyball league
articles.summary: The Nepal Volleyball League has attracted foreign athletes who dominated individual awards, highlighting a noticeable skill gap between them and local players. Rather than viewing this as a disadvantage, coaches and players see the presence of overseas talent as a catalyst for professionalising the sport in Nepal, offering local athletes exposure to higher standards and encouraging the development of training infrastructure.

articles.title: Houthis strike Saudi targets anew as talks over Strait of Hormuz stall
articles.summary: The Houthi movement resumed attacks on Saudi Arabian targets while negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have stalled, heightening concerns that the ongoing Middle East conflict could further threaten global oil supplies.

articles.title: ‘Last Man In Tower’: Ben Rekhi’s film dilutes its source material’s amused cynicism
articles.summary: The Kathmandu Post reviews Ben Rekhi’s film adaptation of Aravind Adiga’s novel “Last Man In Tower.” While the movie is technically competent, the reviewer argues it loses the novel’s sharp, amused cynicism, resulting in a passable but ultimately unsatisfying experience, especially toward the ending.

articles.title: Government rolls out sweeping capital market reform plan
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has unveiled a comprehensive 21-point reform package for the capital market. The plan aims to simplify IPO regulations, restructure the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE), broaden the scope of bond and margin trading, and reduce capital gains tax. These measures are intended to attract more investment, improve market liquidity, and modernize the country's financial infrastructure.

articles.title: Weeks after the Nepal flood disaster, families of the missing hold out hope
articles.summary: Weeks after the devastating floods that struck Nepal, more than 5,130 people remain missing, with hundreds also unaccounted for in neighboring China. Families are tirelessly searching hospitals, contacting authorities, and monitoring online platforms for any sign that their loved ones survived. The article highlights the ongoing anguish, the community's resilience, and the challenges faced by relief agencies as they try to locate and identify the missing amid the lingering aftermath of the disaster.

articles.title: Footbridges rise again from flood wreckage
articles.summary: Repairs and reconstruction have begun on 53 footbridges that were damaged by the August 26 flood along Nepal's Trishuli corridor. The work aims to restore essential connections for local communities, enabling access to markets, schools, health services, and employment opportunities.
